name: Hosea

objectives.text: Identify Hosea as a prophet whom God told to marry Gomer and to keep loving her when she was unfaithful
Retell how Hosea bought Gomer back as a picture of God's love that keeps going for His people
Describe how Hosea pictures God caring for Israel like a parent teaching a little child to walk
Recall that God called His wandering people to return to Him and promised to heal them
Name Hosea's three children and tell what each name means
Explain how God promised to turn 'Not my people' into 'Children of the living God'
Identify Hosea as a prophet sent to the northern kingdom of Israel and locate it on a map of the divided kingdom
Explain why Hosea compares Israel's worship of idols to a wife leaving her husband
Identify the golden calves and foreign alliances in Hosea as ways Israel trusted something other than the Lord
Explain Hosea's charge that God's people were destroyed for lack of knowledge of Him
Explain the image of sowing the wind and reaping the whirlwind as Hosea's picture of the consequences of sin
Write a prayer of confession and return modeled on the words God gives Israel in Hosea 14
Outline the structure of Hosea as a marriage narrative followed by oracles of judgment and hope ending in a call to wisdom
Contrast the shallow repentance of Hosea 6 with the true return of Hosea 14 using the catechism's definition of repentance
Analyze how Hosea develops the marriage metaphor through accusation, discipline, and renewed betrothal
Analyze how the promise of the Valley of Achor as a door of hope reverses the judgment of Joshua 7
Explain how Jesus uses Hosea 6:6 to show that God desires steadfast love rather than empty ritual
Analyze how Hosea's redemption of Gomer foreshadows Christ redeeming His bride the church
Relate Hosea's warnings to the prosperity of Jeroboam II, the political instability that followed, and the fall of Samaria
Explain how the promise that Israel will seek David their king in the latter days points to the Messiah
Analyze how Matthew applies 'Out of Egypt I called my son' to Jesus as the true Son and true Israel
Explain the meaning of hesed in Hosea as God's steadfast covenant love and the loyalty He requires of His people
Analyze how Paul and Peter apply Hosea's reversal of 'Not my people' to Gentiles brought into the church
Analyze how Paul uses Hosea 13:14 to proclaim Christ's victory over death
Analyze how Hosea uses episodes from the life of Jacob to call Israel to repentance
Evaluate how Hosea 11:8-9 portrays God's compassion and holiness, interpreting its language in light of the Reformed confession that God is without passions
Evaluate major interpretations of Hosea's marriage as literal event or vision and the purpose of its shocking prophetic sign act
Synthesize Hosea's marriage message with New Testament bride imagery in a written or oral presentation

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Gomer, buying her back, children's names, idolatry as adultery, marriage metaphor, redemption and Christ, historical context, hesed, sign act, bride imagery). Dropped vague or feeling-oriented filler (love back, forgives when we run away, what unfaithfulness means, apply the call to return). Recast emotional theology as an evaluation of Hosea 11:8-9 anchored to WCF 2.1. Added missing content: Hosea 11 parent imagery, lack of knowledge (ch 4), golden calves and alliances, sowing the wind, shallow versus true repentance, book structure, Valley of Achor, Hosea 6:6 in Matthew, David their king, Matthew 2:15, Romans 9 and 1 Peter 2, 1 Corinthians 15 use of 13:14, Jacob in ch 12, and a prayer of return practice. Added verse-level references and confessional anchors where the doctrine is stated.
